title.narrative: Digital security and digital transformation for journalists

description.narrative:
At least 68 journalists and media workers have been killed in the line of duty in 2024 along, with more than 60% of the killings taking place in countries in conflict - the highest percentage in more than ten years. Recent research indicates that 78% of journalists’ fatalities occur outside of their workplaces, highlighting the pervasive risks journalists face, even in non-conflict zones. On a positive note, 16 countries reported implementing measures to enhance the safety of women journalists, although most crimes against journalists continue to go unpunished. It is also important to note that the safety of journalists encompasses freedom of expression online, directly relating to issues of right-based digital security, surveillance, the right to privacy, and access to information, all of which are pertinent to journalists working in the digital age
In this context, UNESCO will continue to spearhead the implementation of the UN Plan of Action, promoting the protection of journalists at grassroots, national, and global levels, and optimizing the contribution to national strategies and coordination mechanisms. UNESCO will collaborate with national and international stakeholders and other UN entities, including OHCHR, on issues related to standard setting and policymaking, awareness raising and advocacy, monitoring and reporting, research, capacity building, and coalition building. It will especially provide training for the digital challenges facing journalism.
